page.layout: One printed page, one text column with a Greek and Latin verse epigraph at the head. Running head centred at top, page number top right. Marginal notes in the right margin. Catchword at lower right, gathering mark centred below the last line. The left edge shows part of the facing page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Καυσίη, ἡ τ᾽ πάςῃσι[?] μαχέσδοσιν ὄχολον ὅπλον, Καὶ σκέπας ἐν νιφετῷ, ἡδὲ κόρυς ἐν πολέμῳ.

p.i: Causia, quæ Macetum genti fuit vtile tegmen, Pilleus in nimbis, inque acie galea.

main_text.p: Avd. Sed heus, Polybij verba cùm video: atque est, inquit, cùm lupinam aut tale aliquid imponit, tutelæ simul & signi causâ: hærere incipio, vtrum nudo capiti, an galeæ alteri imponat? Eò magis, quòd in Vegetio memini legere: galeas ipsas ad terrorem hirsutis (alij libri vrsinis) pel-libus tectas.Lib. ii. Lips. Non ita hîc factum. cùm præmiserit de simplici tegmine: nec ratio est tam cautè & custoditè armare istos. Addo legere me Galeam venatoriam, pro hoc sensu, in Æmilio Probo, de Datami: Ipse agresti duplicíque amiculo circumdatus, birtáque tunicâ, gerens in capite galeam venatoriam, dextrâ manu clavam.Galea re-natoris. In Data-mi. Ita enim verius distingui, quàm vt ad clavam referatur. Et quídni isti vsi, quibus e cæde ferarum copia? Sed pergo.

„ Habet lignum in longitudine duorum cubitorum.] Sunt igitur in hastili tres pedes. Nam quod in Liuio est: Septena iacula quaternos longa pedes data. & in Fronti-no: Septenis singulos hastis quaternorum circiter pedum armauit: id ad telum totum referendum est, vna cum ferri modo, qui fuit dodrantalis, id est haud longè à pede.Concordia inter Po-lybium & alios.

„ Crassitie vnius digiti.] Ergo tenue lignum, & vt hodiernæ sagittæ. Quídni tale cum septem ea tulerint? supra in Liuij & Frontini verbis habes. Septena igitur illa implebant manum. Huc facit Valerij locus, sed cum nostrâ correctione, qui scribit eos breuibus & incuruis septenis armatos hastis. Breuibus, pedum quattuor: sed quomodo incuruis? an à ferro? non dicit Polybius. &Tenera hasta Vegetius.Valerij locus Lib. ii. cap. iii.

page.notes: The Greek epigraph is set in a Greek type face; the word after πάςῃσι is hard to read and is marked [?]. The Greek line 2 is read with reasonable confidence. The "X" below the text is a gathering mark, taken as signature. Marginal notes in the right margin were placed beside the lines where they stand; the Vegetius and Valerius notes sit together at the end, as they do on the scan. The left-edge fragments belong to the facing page and were left out. Printing errors, such as the odd spacing in "cæde", were left as printed. The hyphens in "pel-libus", "ca-pite", "Fronti-no", "Po-lybium" and "Data-mi" are printed line-end hyphens.
